stewart_read: The rep learns immediately that the person answering is not Ernst, the form-filler, yet proceeds directly into the standard intro and qualifier flow without addressing who she is, whether Ernest is expected to join, or re-anchoring legitimacy for her specifically.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be treating this as routine — many households have someone other than the form-filler answer — and defaulting to continue is a reasonable low-friction choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause on 'this is his sister' and ask directly whether Ernest is available or should be looped in, since he ends up being the only person who can answer the bill question anyway.

quote: Now that, I have to ask Ernest because he is the one staying in it right now.
stewart_read: This is a co-owner-absent-with-data scenario the schema doesn't explicitly cover — it isn't a spouse-decision protocol (no decision being resisted) and isn't quite adult_child_decision_maker (no title/decision framing, just 'he's the one who lives there and knows the bill'). This is a genuine gap: the schema has no protocol for 'the person who can answer the required verify items isn't on the call.'
coaching_implication: Flag to management as a scenario worth adding to protocols: when the qualifying data-holder is a different household member than who's on the phone, the correct move may be to schedule a callback when that person is available rather than pushing through with proxied, uncertain answers.

quote: the cove bill, he said, was around about 140.
stewart_read: A number was captured, but the rep never distinguished on the call that this figure is for a different property (the mother's house) recalled secondhand by the customer's husband — not a confirmed bill for the townhouse being qualified. Treating this as a clean bill capture would overstate what actually happened.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be treating this as a rough proxy figure sufficient to keep the call moving toward the appointment, planning to get the real bill via the text-photo follow-up — a defensible triage move given the account holder was unreachable.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly flag on the call (and in any notes to the closer) that this number is unconfirmed and sourced from an unrelated property, so the number isn't mistaken for real usage data downstream.

quote: Do you have any, bills of mom's Depco's at all?
stewart_read: The customer's search for a bill surfaces a reference to her mother having passed away ('When my mom passed away...') while she digs through paperwork — a vulnerability disclosure the rep does not acknowledge at all in the available transcript.
alternative_hypothesis: Diarization on this stretch is uncertain and largely one-sided customer narration; it's possible the rep responded off-transcript or the moment passed too quickly within her own rambling search to expect a reply, so this may be a lower-severity miss than a clean ignored disclosure.
coaching_implication: Even a brief 'I'm sorry for your loss' costs nothing and the schema treats this as a trust gift; the manager should note this as a soft-skill gap without over-weighting it given the ambiguous, run-on nature of this segment.

quote: Vepco with a b or Pep with a p?
stewart_read: This is a small positive: rather than guessing or moving on with an unclear utility name, the rep confirms spelling precisely, which is useful downstream for accurate utility-specific bill instructions.
coaching_implication: Worth naming in the 1-on-1 as a good habit to keep — precise verification prevents downstream errors without slowing the call down.

quote: do you have a credit score over 6 70 for any all three of you?
stewart_read: This question is being asked of a person who has already said she doesn't know the power bill and can't reach the person who does — asking her to also self-report credit scores for two other people she doesn't speak for compounds an already-unreliable data chain.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may simply be running the standard qualifier list as designed, correctly deferring the accuracy check to the closer's credit pull per the open policy question in qualifiers.credit_qualifier.spencer_operator_note.
coaching_implication: Given the diarization is unclear on who actually answers ('Well, I do. Yeah. Okay. That's fine.'), don't over-coach this single line — but note the pattern of qualifying through a proxy who admits uncertainty on nearly every item.

quote: Alright. You have a great day. Alright. And thank you.
stewart_read: The call ends with pleasantries and no locked appointment day/time, no one-hour block mention, no no-driving/computer instruction, and no 'is that fair?' handshake — button_up is effectively skipped.
alternative_hypothesis: Because the required bill data was never obtained, it may be procedurally correct not to lock a specific appointment time yet — but even so, the rep could have anchored a callback window ('I'll call you back Thursday afternoon') instead of 'whenever.'
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always convert 'I'll call you back' into a specific day/time commitment, even when the appointment itself is pending a document.
